GBV Vault

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
an app which has a secret vault to store pics of abuse, to be used in court

Unique Selling Point:
Last night SA Women Fight back celebrated a year of existence - and the fact that it has just got NPC status -it has 241 000 female members on its private group, and 85 000 facebook members. it has volunteers who have stepped up to support victims through various means - counselling, crisis management, legal assistance, help through the court process. But, and this is the tragic part, the latest statistics show that there has been an increase of domestic abuse and GBV in SA over the last year. This is a story which shows some of the background support it provides and also how it has adapted new technology in the form of a brilliant app which encourages more volunteers to join as "angels" and a system which enables victims - a panic button on the app, and a vault that contains pictures of their abuse. In the private group, women share their sometimes horrific abuse and are supported. Volunteers pour through these messages and reach out to offer support.

Summary:
Recently the organisation mobilised to help Nicole who was abused by her fiance. He had left a note saying that he was going to kill himself and then arrived at her home, threatening her. She was on the phone with the crisis counsellor as he threatened her and luckily police arrived in a few minutes. She had taken out a restraining order against him but he is defending it and she has to prove that he was abused her. But he had destroyed her phone and pictures of her abuse were forever lost.

Enter a new app developed by SA Fight back - which has special features - an emergency number to press for help and nearby SA Women fight back members can respond immediately, , a private chat room which opens immediately so that the victim can report to nominated people what is happening - and most important a vault where women can record images of their abuse over the years, with notes and even medical reports. Only nominated people will have access to this vault which is stored in the cloud, via a password in the event of her death. It also can be used by the victim in court to show a history of abuse. Nicole's pictures were all lost. They would not have been if she had had the vault.Her partner destroyed her phone.

Further information:
We speak to an attorney who devotes a lot of time free of charge to victims - helping them with legal issues.
We speak to Hameen Smith a volunteer crisis counsellor and we see how she worked with victims such as Nicole and others, like organising police assistance, stabilising the situation and providing on going counselling.

We speak to an attorney or a prosecutor to see how useful this app can be in court.

We speak to two other victims who will say that they could not have coped without the support of SA Women Fight back and we speak to a coordinator who describes what goes on in the background to support victims. Angelique was raped after he drink was spiked, and sat for month in shock before her story became known to SA Women Fight back - who then provided both legal and emotional support. SamanthaLee was raped by four men, and again legal and emotional support was provided.

But we also hear from an emotional Bronwyn Litkie who started the organisation - at just how overwhelmed all the volunteers can feel, and this app is their way hopefully of attracting new volunteers in the form of angels who can volunteer their services to assist victims.

He had left a note saying that he was going to kill himself and then arrived at her home, threatening her. She was on the phone with the crisis counsellor as he threatened her and luckily police arrived in a few minutes. She had taken out a restraining order against him but he is defending it and she has to prove that he was abused her. But he had destroyed her phone and pictures of her abuse were forever lost. Enter a new app developed by SA Fight back - which has special features - an emergency number to press for help and nearby SA Women fight back members can respond immediately, , a private chat room which opens immediately so that the victim can report to nominated people what is happening - and most important a vault where women can record images of their abuse over the years, with notes and even medical reports. Only nominated people will have access to this vault which is stored in the cloud, via a password in the event of her death. It also can be used by the victim in court to show a history of abuse. Nicole's pictures were all lost. They would not have been if she had had the vault.Her partner destroyed her phone.
metadata.Further information: We speak to an attorney who devotes a lot of time free of charge to victims - helping them with legal issues. We speak to Hameen Smith a volunteer crisis counsellor and we see how she worked with victims such as Nicole and others, like organising police assistance, stabilising the situation and providing on going counselling. We speak to an attorney or a prosecutor to see how useful this app can be in court. We speak to two other victims who will say that they could not have coped without the support of SA Women Fight back and we speak to a coordinator who describes what goes on in the background to support victims. Angelique was raped after he drink was spiked, and sat for month in shock before her story became known to SA Women Fight back - who then provided both legal and emotional support. SamanthaLee was raped by four men, and again legal and emotional support was provided. But we also hear from an emotional Bronwyn Litkie who started the organisation - at just how overwhelmed all the volunteers can feel, and this app is their way hopefully of attracting new volunteers in the form of angels who can volunteer their services to assist victims.
